assess-team-dimension: Worker skill dispatched only by assess-team (six parallel dimension runs); its six output files, scores and caps are checked by the assess-team eval, so a standalone eval would duplicate that one.
ensemble-assess: Pure keyword dispatcher (repo, team, config, report, repo --only <dimension>) that loads another assessment skill and re-implements none of its logic; the target skills have or need their own evals.
ensemble-author-playwright-tests: An interactive session with a QA engineer that runs each test against a live QA environment and syncs results to Azure DevOps test plans and tasks, so it cannot run non-interactively or offline and its outputs live in an external service.
ensemble-feature: Pure dispatcher that only builds a /ensemble:new-feature invocation and then hands off to the ensemble-new-feature stage machine (run state, PRD/TRD, beads, PR stages), so it produces no artifact of its own that an offline script can check.
ensemble-issue: Pure keyword router that only hands off to the fix-issue and list-issue skills (which need br/bv, gh and a live issue run); its only own behaviour is a keyword-table print on no match, so there is nothing script-checkable that is not the delegated skills' behaviour.
ensemble-release: Orchestrates a real release: deploys to staging and canary-then-100% production through a deployment orchestrator, monitors live error rate and health checks, publishes a GitHub release and can roll production back, none of which a stub can stand in for honestly, and --dry-run is documented as a future enhancement.
ensemble-reqnroll: Pure keyword dispatcher (features, feature-drift, bindings, binding-drift, tdd) that reads and follows a sibling command's SKILL.md and re-implements none of it; each target has or needs its own eval, and the only own behaviour is printing a keyword table on no match.
ensemble-reqnroll-tdd: Its core is a red-then-green gate that builds and runs a .NET xUnit project (dotnet restore needs the NuGet network) while delegating to two other agents, so nothing offline and deterministic remains to check beyond what the ensemble-generate-reqnroll-bindings and reqnroll evals already cover.
ensemble-standards: Pure keyword dispatcher (discover, inject, fold) that hands off to the sibling standards commands and re-implements none of their phases; the targets have or need their own evals and the only own behaviour is a keyword-table print on no match.
ensemble-trd: Pure keyword dispatcher over the TRD-adjacent commands (create, refine, implement, analyze, complexity, validate, verify, status, graph) that forwards to the sibling SKILL.md and re-implements none of it; each target has or needs its own eval and the only own behaviour is a keyword-table print on no match.
implement-trd-tasks-reference: On-demand reference (sections 1-7) that /ensemble:implement-trd-tasks reads on pointer, explicitly 'not a standalone workflow', so it has no behaviour of its own to run; its rules are exercised only through the commands that read it.
staleness-gate: Procedural gate whose outcome depends on wall-clock file mtimes (a TRD older than 24h or source files newer than it) and on the exit status of the model-driven /ensemble:refine-trd command, and which writes no artifact, so a deterministic offline eval cannot honestly set up or check it.
